Supplementary Fig. S2 Enrichment of CD36+ pro-inflammatory macrophage in cancer
correlates with poor outcome of patients with PTC. A, Heatmap showing top marker
genes (obtained from unsupervised clustering) used for custom classification of the
myeloid compartment. B, Comparison of the absolute infiltration proportion of CD36+
macrophages between paired peritumor tissues and tumor tissues in the TCGA-THCA

cohort (n = 58 clinical samples). Data are represented as mean ± SEM. A paired
Student's t-test was used to assess the difference. ***, P = 0.0006. C, Representative
gating strategy of CD36+ macrophages in peritumor tissues and tumor tissues from
patients with PTC. D, IHC staining of SPP1 expression in PTC tissues (scale bar: 50
μm). E, A representative result of IHC staining of SPP1 expression in paired PTC tissue
and peritumor tissue. F, Bar plot showing proportion of the relative protein levels of
SPP1 in 28 paired PTC and peritumor tissues as measured by IHC staining. G, A
representative result of IHC staining of CD68 expression in paired PTC tissue and
peritumor tissue. H, Table showing relationship between CD68 expression and clinicopathologic characteristics in patients with PTC. I, Bar plot showing proportion of the
relative protein levels of CD68 in 28 paired PTC and peritumor tissues as measured by
IHC staining. J, Correlation analysis between the expression level of SPP1 and the
infiltration level of pro-inflammatory and anti-inflammatory macrophages in thyroid
cancer. K, Heatmap displaying metabolic pathway activity scores in each macrophage
subtype.
